newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan buys one Oct jet cargo, considers a second.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan buys one Oct jet cargo, considers a second.

text.p: State-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has bought one jet fuel October cargo and is considering awarding a second cargo, a company official said on Wednesday.
CPC bought one cargo at around $244 per tonne cost-and-freight (c-and-f) Taiwan and "may buy another cargo tomorrow", the official said.
Sources said CPC may buy the second cargo due to the unexpected shutdown of one crude distillation unit (CDU) at the Taoyuan refinery earlier this week.
The 120,000 barrel-per-day CDU was closed following a pipeline problem.

The official said CPC may buy the second cargo on a floating basis. Trading sources said that CPC had received offers on a floating basis at about $1.00-$1.10 per barrel over the prevailing Singapore spot quotes.
Traders said the current spot market for jet fuel to North Asia was about $1.50-$1.75 per barrel over Singapore spot quotes on a c-and-f basis.
The tender sought 32,000 tonnes of jet fuel for delivery during October 1-31, c-and-f Keelung or Shen Ao. It closed on September 17 and offers were valid until September 19.
CPC had earlier cancelled a tender to buy jet fuel for delivery in October due to high offers which ranged from just under $250 to more than $260 per tonne c-and-f basis.
The latest tender gave sellers the option of offering on a floating basis against prevailing published Singapore spot quotes, which had not been CPC's practice in the past.
